## Setting
Award of a national grant for basic research in the life sciences. A five-member review panel convened by a national funding agency deliberates over the proposals that reached the final round. One multi-year grant is awarded in this cycle. Participants: Benjamin, Midori, Shizue, Victoria and Ryuji. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Travel and bench-fee lines in the ledgers
- National computing agreement and facility day rates
- Incident logs on shared instrumentation
- Station records from partner field sites
- Closeout files of finished awards
- Portfolio review of schedule overruns
- Accreditation and bookings at shared facilities
- National repository deposit turnaround
- Staffing rolls for technical posts
- Minutes on secondments and crew strength

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Shizue, Ryuji, Victoria, Benjamin and Midori. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the candidates | 4 turns | every participant votes; the candidate with the most votes is selected |
- Several participants may choose the same thing; what is found out is told only to the participant who looked into it.
If votes are tied, one of the tied candidates is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

## Your profile
Name: Shizue
Age: 78
Gender: female
Personality: Shizue has a very calm and gentle personality. Even as she has grown older, she continues to smile warmly at those around her and is a very caring person. She is always considerate of others, friendly, and sometimes shows a playful side. She often reaches out to those who are feeling down with kind words and never hesitates to lend a helping hand when needed, which has earned her the affection of many people in the village and community. Through her years of life experience, Shizue has come to understand the importance of living peacefully with others.
Concern: Our judgements about promise have not aged well, and some of us have watched confident picks quietly stall while plainer ones kept earning their keep. Rather than trust that instinct once more, I went back through what finished awards here actually delivered and when.

## Plan
The discussion follows this plan.
- Round 1: The panel discusses the necessity of verifying operational feasibility before selecting a proposal. They agree to divide the available administrative and technical records to identify potential bottlenecks.
- Round 2: Participants share their findings regarding facility availability, staffing shortages, and historical success rates. They debate whether theoretical promise outweighs practical constraints.
- Round 3: The panel evaluates the candidates against the discovered constraints. They weigh the risks of facility bottlenecks and staffing gaps against the potential for long-term impact.

Each participant's part:
- Shizue: Cares about the long-term delivery of results. She looks for projects that mirror historically successful, steady patterns of output.
